issues.issue: Should the Court answer the first certified question on whether the lock-in principle applies to family members of skilled worker applicants?
issues.applicant_position: Minister: visa officers decide on the facts as they exist when they assess an application, unless the statute clearly displaces that.
issues.respondent_position: Hamids: the lock-in principle should guide interpretation of the Regulations, so eligibility is fixed at the date of application.
issues.result_quote: In order to decide this appeal it is not necessary to answer the first and more general question

issues.issue: Must a child aged 22 or over meet the dependent-child criteria of financial dependence and full-time study when the visa officer assesses the application, not only when it was made?
issues.applicant_position: Minister: the dependent-child criteria must be met when the visa application is assessed, so the officer correctly removed the sons.
issues.respondent_position: Hamids: the sons qualified when the application was made, and later loss of student status should not defeat their eligibility.
issues.result_quote: cannot be included as part of his or her parent's application for permanent residence in Canada.

issues.issue: Does the lock-in principle require student status to be fixed at the date of the visa application?
issues.applicant_position: Minister: lock-in does not extend to student status; age is locked in only as a policy exception and the other criteria are not.
issues.respondent_position: Hamids: student status should be locked in like age, since there is no rational basis for treating the two differently.
issues.result_quote: it is not anomalous to interpret sections 84 and 85 as requiring that a child aged 22 or over is financially dependent and a student
